Three findings together permit one disease: tri-lineage cytopenia, diaphyseal bone pain and diffuse nontender adenopathy with splenomegaly. That is marrow replacement, and marrow replacement is confirmed in the marrow.

Confirms, or diagnostic selects the bone marrow aspirate. The CBC makes you suspect leukemia; the marrow proves it.

edits.find:
The word doing the work is spherocytes: on a board smear they have exactly two owners, hereditary spherocytosis and warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia. The negative Coombs settles that fork — antibody-coated cells are excluded, so the spherocytes are a membrane defect. MCHC 38% and the affected father corroborate; neither is the decider.

The last move is a mapping rather than a diagnosis. The options are tests, so name the disease and then name its assay: eosin-5-maleimide binding, with osmotic fragility as the older equivalent. Choosing CD55/CD59 is a stored-outcome error — Coombs-negative hemolysis retrieved as a conclusion rather than as a question, so the three findings that fail PNH here (normal white cells and platelets, spherocytes, an affected father) were never asked.
